title: Domain of a Fractional-Power Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The function F(x)=x^(2/3) can be read as the square of the cube root of x. Find its natural domain.

steps.title: Rewrite Using Radical Notation
steps.explanation: The 2/3 power means: take the cube root first (denominator 3), then square (numerator 2).
steps.why: For rational exponents m/n, x^(m/n) = (n-th root of x)^m whenever the root exists.

steps.title: Check the Cube Root
steps.explanation: Odd roots are defined for negative, zero, and positive inputs, so the cube root step never fails.
steps.why: Unlike even roots, odd roots of negative numbers are real (e.g. cube root of -8 is -2).

steps.title: Check the Squaring Step
steps.explanation: Squaring any real number produces a real number, so the outer operation also imposes no restriction.
steps.why: Powers with positive integer exponents are defined everywhere on the reals.

steps.title: Conclude the Domain
steps.explanation: Both stages work for every real x, so nothing must be excluded.
steps.why: No even root, denominator, or logarithm appears, hence the full real line is the domain.
